heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P handles Polymaker PolyMax PETG natively without hardware upgrades, achieving reliable production speeds up to 167 mm/s capped at a 14 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. Thanks to the open-frame design and stock stainless steel nozzle, thermal creep is minimized while maximizing interlayer toughness.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate with a thin PVP glue stick layer as a release agent
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 14 mm³/s in the filament profile to cap continuous high-speed flow and prevent cold extrusion under-extrusion.
Enable Wipe While Retracting with a 1 mm wipe distance to minimize fine PETG stringing and nozzle accumulation during travel moves.
Adjust Pressure Advance (PA / Flow Dynamics) to approximately 0.038 s to sharpen corners without bulging or seam pockmarks.
Keep Part Cooling Fan between 20% min and 50% max, with Keep Fan Always On enabled to balance layer bonding strength against bridging performance.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Stringing and fine whisker buildup on the nozzle
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PolyMax PETG is hygroscopic and prone to oozing at 243°C when slight ambient moisture is present, coupled with insufficient direct-drive retraction wiping.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dry the filament spool at 65°C for 6 hours; in OrcaSlicer, enable Wipe on Loops and set retraction to 0.8 mm at 35 mm/s.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: PEI sheet damage or excessive bed adhesion tearing the coating
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: PolyMax PETG forms a chemical molecular bond with smooth or textured PEI surfaces when printed directly at 75°C without an interface layer.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Apply a uniform layer of liquid glue or PVP glue stick to act as an sacrificial release agent, and allow the bed to cool below 35°C before removing parts.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Weak interlayer adhesion or brittle parts along the Z-axis
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Over-cooling from the print head auxiliary fan or excessive primary part fan speed quenching extruded layers too quickly.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Turn off the auxiliary chamber fan completely and clamp maximum part cooling fan speed to 50%.

faq.question: Can I print Polymaker PolyMax PETG with the P1P stock stainless steel nozzle?
faq.answer: Yes. PolyMax PETG is completely non-abrasive and prints reliably using the stock 0.4 mm stainless steel nozzle without causing premature wear.

faq.question: Does printing PolyMax PETG on the P1P require an enclosure?
faq.answer: No, an enclosure is not required. In fact, printing PETG in an open-frame printer like the P1P is advantageous as it prevents excessive chamber heat from causing heat creep.

faq.question: Why is my print speed capped at 167 mm/s?
faq.answer: The 167 mm/s limit is calculated from the filament's safe maximum volumetric flow rate of 14 mm³/s at standard 0.42 mm line width and 0.20 mm layer height to prevent nozzle starvation.

faq.question: Do I need to dry Polymaker PolyMax PETG straight out of the vacuum-sealed bag?
faq.answer: Yes, PETG is inherently hygroscopic. Drying it at 65°C for 6 hours before printing significantly reduces stringing, improves surface finish, and eliminates popping sounds at the nozzle.
